- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed prior 3-day average by more than 2%.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period (last 10 days) prices; cap forecast at 10% below true outcome for final 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.0, 0.0, 1.0), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment direction for next 3–5 days.
